from_notes: The stomach has four parts: the cardiac portion, the fundic region, the body and the pyloric portion; the alimentary canal walls have four layers: serosa (outermost), muscularis, sub-mucosa and mucosa.
x: Serosa is the outermost layer of the wall of the alimentary canal, not a region of the stomach. The stomach's regions are the cardiac part (where the oesophagus opens), the fundus, the body and the pyloric part (which opens into the duodenum).
source: PMF General Science 02 p.39 (stomach: cardiac, fundic, body, pyloric) and p.40 (layers: serosa outermost); Rocket Biology p.47-49 (stomach in the digestive system)

from_notes: Universal Recipient: People with blood group AB can receive blood from any group because they lack A or B antibodies.
x: Group AB is the universal recipient: its plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so it can receive red cells of any ABO group. O is the universal donor (its red cells carry no A or B antigen).
source: Rocket Biology p.52 (AB: antigens A+B, plasma antibody none; O: no antigen); PMF General Science 02 p.27 (AB = universal recipient)
